advanced: Advanced mode lets you type any value, also outside the normal range, and shows extra settings. Each stage remembers its own on/off.
fitMode: How the plate meets the robot flange. Plate: flat plate only (easiest to print, weaker centring). Plate + Spigot: adds a short tube that goes into the flange centre hole. Plate + Spigot + Collar: also a collar around the flange raised spigot. Options your flange cannot take are greyed out.
spigot: Holed: the spigot is a tube, bore = spigot - 2 x thickness (lighter, uses less plastic). Full: a solid cylinder (stiffer). In Plate mode there is no spigot: Holed keeps a hole over the flange centre hole, Full closes the plate.
dowel: The dowel stops the plate from rotating on the flange. Hole: a hole for a metal dowel pin (best). Printed pin: a pin printed with the part (weaker and less accurate).
wallKeys: Some flanges have small pockets in a wall. With this on, the plate gets matching keys that lock into them.
thickness: Wall and plate thickness in mm, used for the plate, the spigot wall and the collar wall. Green = recommended range.
headSeat: Cut for the screw heads on the face away from the robot. None: flat. Countersink: cone-shaped seat for flat-head screws. Counterbore: round pocket for socket-head screws.
plateMargin: Extra material between the screw heads and the plate edge, in mm. Green = recommended range.
tolerances: How much each surface is offset so printed parts fit. A hole gets bigger by 2× the value in diameter, a peg gets smaller by 2× the value. Green = recommended, red = not recommended. Print a test piece when you change printer or material.
primitiveSize: Cube: edge length. Cylinder and cone: diameter and height. Sphere and the other solids: overall diameter. The type and size are used by "Add primitive", which always adds a new object. To change an object's size later, delete it and add a new one.
moveRotate: Click an object in the 3D view or in the Objects list to select it. Arrows move it, rings rotate it. Type any value in the boxes. Position is an offset from where the file placed the part: 0 = exactly as in your CAD file. Rotation turns the part around that same origin point. Ctrl+Z undoes a move.
space: World axes: the arrows always point along the scene's X, Y and Z, so a part tilted by 30° still moves straight up when you drag the Z arrow. Part axes: the arrows are tilted with the part, so you push it along its own sides. The numbers in the boxes are always in world axes.
robotClearance: Keep-out cylinder below the robot side: the plate diameter plus this value on each side. Nothing grows inside it, so the connector leaves room around the robot flange and its cables.
gapObjects: Extra gap around every avoided object. The connector stays this far away from it. 0 = only the object itself.
gapFaces: Extra gap in front of every avoided face. The red zone is pushed outward by this amount. 0 = only the face itself.
clickTool: Pick what a left-click does. Connect face (green): the connector attaches to this face; works on any tool object. Avoid face (red): nothing grows into the face, and the gap number pushes the zone outward. Avoid object (red): the whole object is kept clear, grown by the gap number. Right-click clears a green or red item. Shift-click is a shortcut for the avoid mode.
boltClearance: Keeps room above the screw heads so a screwdriver can reach them. Diameter is the screw head plus margin. It covers the whole screw through the plate, including a countersink or counterbore. Height is counted from the top face of the tool start; by default it equals the head diameter. Slot runs the clearance outward from the flange centre so inner screws stay reachable; Cylinder keeps clear only straight above each head. The numbers show the real size in mm.
printable: Prints with the flange face on the bed and no supports: nothing grows below the bed, and every part rests on material below it (45° overhang at most). Test feature.
bridge: Bridge is instant: a solid wrap from the flange top to the green faces, narrower in the middle, minus the red zones, the robot side, Flange Clearance and Bolt Clearance. It updates by itself after every change. Waist: how much narrower the middle is than a straight wrap (0 = straight).
smoothing: Each Smooth click rounds the voxel steps a little more and keeps the volume. Connect surfaces stay in place. Smoothing fills the red zones a little, so finish with Re-cut clearances. Generate resets smoothing.
reCut: Cuts the clearance zones out of the final shape again, like a boolean difference. Connect surfaces are never cut. Use it after smoothing, or after changing a gap.
refinement: Always start with Draft: it designs the connector and clears the red zones, fast. Normal and Fine then refine that Draft on a finer voxel. Normal unlocks after Draft has finished, Fine after Normal (hover a greyed button to see what is needed). Finished levels are kept, so you can click between Draft, Normal and Fine to compare them. If you change the objects, faces, clearances or the load settings, you start again at Draft.
materialAmount: How much of the design space may be filled with material. More = stronger and heavier. The grams next to it are an estimate of the first-pass weight (design space volume × amount × PLA density); the real result is shown after Generate. Green = recommended range.
voxelTarget: Voxel size of the Fine level, in mm. Smaller = more detail but much slower. Normal is halfway between the Draft voxel (about 1.5 mm) and this value. Example: target 1.0 gives Normal 1.25 and Fine 1.0.
